To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a method for the estimation of binding free energy of protein-ligand complexes using MD in vacuo and continuum electrostatic calculations.

the binding free energy of protein-ligand interactions can be estimated by molecular mechanics and electrostatics, and that the method can be used to design inhibitors with improved binding affinities for proteins of unknown structure.
the method provides a good estimate of binding free energy and is robust enough to provide a reliable ranking of the binding affinity of a series of ligands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the estimation of binding free energies of interaction between a protein and a small ligand.
the development of a method for the estimation of protein-ligand binding affinity using molecular mechanics and a continuum electrostatic model.
the development of a new approach to the estimation of the absolute binding free energy between proteins and ligand molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the absence of any better approach, the proposed method can be used with a good degree of confidence to estimate absolute binding free energies of interaction between proteins (or nucleic acids) and ligands.
the method is a useful and reliable tool for the calculation of binding free energy of small ligands to proteins, provided the protein structure is available.
the method is able to provide a reliable estimation of the binding free energies of HIV-1 proteases and inhibitors, and that the method is also applicable to other protein-ligand complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a method for the calculation of absolute binding free energies that does not require reparametrization for new protein targets and can be used with complexes of unknown 2D or 3D structure.
the method is a good predictor of binding free energies for the HIV-1 proteases and their ligands.
this method is able to estimate the binding free energy of a protein-ligand system from the 3D structure of the complex with a reasonable accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding free energies calculated with our method correlate well with the experimental binding free energies, even when the protein-ligands complex structure is not known.
the method provides a reliable and fast estimation of the absolute binding free energy for protein-ligand interactions, which can be useful for virtual screening and for the design of novel drugs.

the method is able to predict absolute binding free energy values for a set of unknown structures with an unsigned mean unsigned error of 0·8 kcal/mol, which is a satisfactory performance in view of the fact that the method uses no experimental data for the set of unknown structures.
